US-linked financials (HOOD, VRNA) outperform on retail trading volumes and biotech financing cycles, offering diversification from domestic Indonesian credit risk.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's domestic coal demand remains structurally supported by the government's push for energy self-sufficiency and new smelter capacity, insulating local miners from global price swings.
Nickel processing mandates and downstreaming policies continue to create durable premiums for integrated Indonesian players over raw ore exporters, driving relative outperformance.
The IDX energy complex is benefiting from a persistent domestic liquidity bid, while US-listed energy names face higher rate sensitivity and weaker investor appetite, widening the arbitrage.

US-exposed consumer names lag due to weak American demand and FX headwinds, reinforcing a home-market bias for Indonesian investors.
sectors.ai: Buy selective mid-cap consumer names riding domestic volume recovery and Ramadan restocking, led by IATA and IMAS; avoid US-exposed FMCG laggards. Position into KING and SRSN for staple resilience, but trim OLIV on valuation. Expect continued dispersion favoring local-branded staples over multinationals through Q2.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's healthcare spending is structurally rising on JKN coverage expansion and an aging population, underpinning sustained demand for hospitals and diagnostics operators like RSCH and DGNS.

US-linked healthcare suppliers (WIRG, OMED) face headwinds from slower US reimbursement and tariff-driven costs, making domestic-revenue pure plays the preferred exposure.
sectors.ai: Buy selective healthcare names on domestic demand strength, led by PYFA, RSCH, and DGNS, while KLBF offers core stability. US-linked exposure (WIRG, OMED) is a drag; rotate toward pure-play local operators. Signal is NORMAL, so add on dips, not chase. Target RSCH and DGNS for near-term momentum; KLBF for defensive compounding.

sectors.name: Logistics

Fuel price volatility and rupiah depreciation create a bifurcation: asset-heavy sea/port logistics outperform while airline and land transport margins compress, favoring selective stock picking.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to Indonesia logistics on the back of port-operator SAFE and trucking TRUK limit-up moves, which signal domestic volume inflection ahead of peak season. Favor names with port or multimodal assets (SAFE, PPGL, SMDR) over airline laggards (GIAA, TAXI) given fuel cost drag. Trim US-linked names if global trade softens; maintain WATCH for pullback entries.
